title: High blood sugar (prediabetes): how to plan your daily plate
intro: When the doctor says your blood sugar is a bit high, many people start to worry straight away. Take a deep breath first. This is a good time to start making small changes. You don't need to give up rice or kuih completely. The key is how you plan your plate, your portion sizes and moving after meals.

sections.h: What slightly high blood sugar means
sections.p: It means your body is starting to be less efficient at controlling sugar. Only a doctor can confirm this through a blood test. Many people can help control their readings by changing how they eat and move. But everyone is different, so keep going for check-ups as your doctor advises.

sections.h: An easy way: the quarter plate
sections.p: Imagine your plate divided into four. Half the plate is vegetables. A quarter is protein like fish, chicken, eggs or tauhu. The other quarter is rice, noodles or bread. For rice, that's roughly one normal senduk (rice scoop). You can use this at home, at a warung or at nasi campur.

A glass of teh tarik or kopi susu may have an estimated 2 to 4 teaspoons of sugar. Sirap and packet drinks are also high in sugar. Try asking for kurang manis (less sweet) first, then slowly switch to kosong (no sugar). Warm water, teh o kosong or kopi o kosong are good choices.

sections.h: The order you eat in helps too
sections.p: Try eating your vegetables and dishes first, then the rice. Many people find they feel full faster and don't add more rice. You can eat kuih and sweet fruit, but have a little, ideally after your main meal, not on an empty stomach.

Walking 10 to 15 minutes after a meal can help your body use the sugar in your blood. No need to go fast. Walk around the house, to the surau, or to a nearby shop. If it's raining, march on the spot while watching TV.

action: Fill half your plate with vegetables at lunch and dinner.
Order your drink kurang manis (less sweet) or kosong (no sugar), starting with one glass a day.
Eat vegetables and dishes first, then rice.
Walk 10 minutes after your biggest meal of the day.
Save kuih or biscuits for the weekend, or take only half.
doctor: See your doctor first if you are often thirsty, pee often, lose weight for no reason, have blurred vision, wounds that heal slowly, or numbness in your feet. Also see your doctor before making big changes to how you eat or starting exercise if you have heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or are taking any medicine. Don't start, change or stop medicine on your own. Discuss with your doctor.

faq.q: Do I have to stop eating rice completely?
faq.a: No need. Reduce your portion to about one senduk, and make sure you have lots of vegetables and a protein dish. You can also try brown rice or rice mixed with vegetables if you like.

faq.q: Can't I eat fruit because it's sweet?
faq.a: You can eat fruit. Have one serving at a time, for example a slice of papaya or one medium apple. Avoid fruit juice because the sugar goes in faster and it's less filling.

faq.q: Is brown sugar or honey better than white sugar?
faq.a: They are all still sugar. The effect on blood sugar is almost the same. It's better to cut down your total sugar, whatever the type.
